Duration::abs¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

Duration Duration::abs() const;

What It Does¶

Returns the magnitude of each element, discarding direction — negative durations, built from e.g. pluss::duration::minutes(-15), become positive.

Parameters¶

None — this is a zero-argument accessor on self.

Returns¶

Duration A new duration holding the elementwise absolute value.

Examples¶

Example 1. abs() on a negative duration.

auto neg_fifteen_min = pluss::duration::minutes(-15);
std::cout << pluss::duration::print(neg_fifteen_min.abs());

Output¶

Duration(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1)
0 days 00:15:00.000000000

abs(-15 min) = 15 min, with the leading - gone from the printed form.

Notes¶

  • abs() returns a Duration, not a Series — unlike the comparison family, it stays in duration-space.

  • abs(d) is equivalent to d if d.ge(pluss::duration::nanos(0)) else -d, but computed directly.

See Also¶

  • sign: direction alone, the complementary piece of information abs discards.

  • clip: bounding into a range, another unary transform.

  • neg: unary negation.
